dialogue.shona: Nyama iyi yakaoma chaizvo pakubikwa kwayo.
dialogue.english: This meat became very tough when it was cooked.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Nyama [meat] • iyi [iyi] • yakaoma [it (past) oma] • chaizvo [very much / truly] • pakubikwa [on / at kubikwa] • kwayo [kwayo]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('yakaoma')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'yakaoma' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: How Shona Sentences Fit Together (Subject + Tense + Verb)
grammar_notes.content: In 'Nyama iyi yakaoma chaizvo pakubikwa kwayo.', notice how a single Shona verb word packs together who is doing the action (the subject prefix), when it happens (the tense marker), and the action itself (the verb stem). Once you recognize the building blocks at the start of the verb—like 'ndi-' (I), 'u-' (you), 'ti-' (we), or 'va-' (they)—you can immediately spot the subject even when no separate pronoun word is used!
grammar_notes.rule: [Who (Subject Prefix)] + [When (Tense Marker)] + [Action (Verb Root)] -> e.g., ti- (we) + -cha- (will) + -svika (arrive) = tichasvika

grammar_notes.title: Describing Nouns: Word Order in Shona
grammar_notes.content: In English, descriptive words like adjectives, possessives ('my', 'our'), demonstratives ('this', 'that'), and numbers come BEFORE the noun ('this big house', 'my two books'). In Shona, the noun always comes FIRST, and all descriptive words follow right after it! For example: 'nyama iyi' ('this meat'), 'mwana uyu' ('this child'), 'goho guru' ('a big harvest'), and 'makomo marefu' ('tall mountains').
grammar_notes.rule: Noun FIRST + Descriptor SECOND -> mota iyi (this car), mabhuku edu (our books), makomo marefu (tall mountains)

cultural_notes.title: Zimbabwean Cuisine: Sadza, Relish & Traditional Foods
cultural_notes.content: At the heart of Zimbabwean home cooking is 'sadza'—a thick, smooth porridge made from white maize meal ('hupfu') cooked with water. Sadza is always served with a savoury accompaniment called 'usavi' (relish), most commonly leafy green vegetables ('muriwo') sautéed with tomatoes, onions, and cooking oil ('mafuta'), or meat ('nyama'). Beloved traditional delicacies also include roasted groundnuts ('nzungu'), cowpeas ('nyemba'), and protein-rich mopane caterpillars ('madora') pan-roasted with tomatoes and onions.

active_exercises.prompt: Complete this new sentence in the past tense: 'Nezuro amai ______ sadza nenyama.' (Yesterday Mother cooked sadza and meat.)
active_exercises.explanation: 'Amai' takes the respectful plural past prefix 'vaka-' + '-bika' (cook) -> 'vakabika' ('cooked').

Milk or water because they feel thirsty
Maize meal and cooking oil from the market
Salt and vegetables for the evening meal
active_exercises.correct_answer: Milk or water because they feel thirsty

active_exercises.prompt: Choose the right locative prefix: You want to say 'The keys are ON the table' ('______tafura').
active_exercises.explanation: The prefix 'pa-' means 'on / at a specific surface', so 'pa-' + 'tafura' = 'patafura' ('on the table').
